g.text: Rendered evidence from captured output
1705-`--all-targets` expands **one axis**: attached environments if the suite has
1706-any, otherwise attached clients — never a cross product, because an environment
1707-already resolves a client. It starts **one paid run per target**, launched as a
1708-single group that occupies one concurrency slot rather than N.
1710-`--environment` / `--client` and `--server` are mutually exclusive: an
1711-environment or client supplies a closed server set that an override cannot
1712-change.
1714-> [!WARNING]
1716-> `--refresh-snapshot` **changes the suite**, not just this run: it re-derives
1717-> and stores the suite's host-config snapshot, so every future run uses the new
1718-> one. It is rejected on any multi-target launch — several runs racing to write
1719-> one snapshot would leave the suite pinned to whichever finished last.
1721-#### Output and exit codes
1723-With `--format json`, stdout is **exactly one JSON document** — the launch
1724-receipt, with nothing appended — so CI can parse it directly. In human format
1725-the CLI prints a `View:` link per started run, a `Started N/M runs (group …)`
1726-summary when several launched, and a `Failed: <target> — <code>: <message>`
1727-line per failure.
1729-With `--wait`, the default output contains the launch receipt and completed
1851:mcpjam cloud eval run --file .mcpjam/evals/s_billing.yaml \
1852- --allow-approximated c_refund_partial \
1853- --approval-reason "Reviewed against the upstream rubric; ENG-4821"
1856-Checked before anything is billed, each with its own message: approving a
1857-**native** case (nothing to approve), a **claimed-exact** one (needs no
1858-approval), an **unsupported** or **unresolved** one (approval covers a case
1859-whose behaviour was approximated, not one whose behaviour is missing), a
1860-**disabled** or **unselected** one (the run will not execute it), an unknown
1861-id, or the same id twice. The flags are refused outright with `--suite`: a
1862-hosted suite's cases are not the ones this invocation authored, so an
1863-authored-id selector has nothing to resolve against.
1865-**The approval belongs to the run, never to the case.** You supply an id and a
1866-reason and nothing else — the approver and the timestamp are derived by the
1867-server and frozen into that run's own snapshot, because a caller-supplied
1868-approver would file one person's approval under another's name and a
1869-caller-supplied timestamp could be backdated past the edit that invalidated the
1870-claim. Nothing persists: edit the suite, re-sync, or launch again, and the flags
1871-are required again.
